Jason — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in David (legal) and Lauren/Ben for ops/tech routing.

High level options from Redwood we typically propose (short version):
1) Regulatory request path — Customer provides regulator notice; Redwood provides an evidence package (witnessed snapshot + attachable metadata) within a defined window.
2) Material incident path — internal trigger where Redwood may be asked to provide broader access (witness + timed console access) and customer must approve auditor scope.

Points we should confirm in the Order Form / Exhibit:
- Trigger definitions (Regulatory request vs. Material Incident vs. Court order).
- Notification timelines (standard: 10 business days; expedited: 72 hours for emergencies).
- Delivery modes: (a) KMS-wrapped snapshot delivered to customer; (b) Witnessed validation with TrustAudits-style third-party present; (c) Onsite/offline handover for air-gapped installs.
- Cost allocation (who pays for auditor travel / escrow services).
- Data retention and redaction scope for PII/PHI.

I'll ask David to draft language we can insert into an Order Form exhibit. Ben and Lauren — can you sketch an evidence-routing diagram (simple) and confirm operational constraints (windows we can commit to) so we can include a practical SLA?

Subject: RE: Question on Order Form exhibit — on-prem audit trigger and evidence routing

Jason / team — attaching a tracked draft of an Exhibit and a redline of the Order Form clause (attachments). High-level legal positions we recommend:

- Trigger: split into (i) "Regulatory Request" (formal written request by a competent regulator) and (ii) "Qualified Incident" (defined severity + evidence of impact). We avoid catch-all "material" language.
- Notification: 10 business days standard; allow a 72-hour emergency escalation if regulator demands immediate access (customer must certify emergency).
- Evidence delivery: Redwood will provide a KMS-wrapped snapshot to the customer within the notification window. For third-party auditors, either (A) customer receives snapshot and verifies, or (B) Redwood facilitates a witnessed session where the auditor (or TrustAudits) is present and signs an evidence receipt certificate. We do not routinely decrypt customer KMS keys — unwrapping is customer-managed or performed under a supervised witness protocol.
- Custody/escrow-lite: propose an "escrow-lite" exhibit where a sealed snapshot is deposited with a mutually approved steward (cost borne by customer unless otherwise agreed).
- Payment and scope: any auditor travel or extraordinary effort is billable per the Order Form; standard witness sessions (remote) included as part of Private Deployment support.
- Retention: evidence retention period default 180 days; extended retention negotiable.

I've preserved a short fallback clause that allows Redwood to provide console/log extracts if the formal snapshot path is infeasible.

Next steps: Naomi / Ops to confirm timeline and what we can operationally promise. Jason / BrightLine to indicate preference for (A) snapshot-to-customer or (B) witnessed-audit.

Regards,
David Kim
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Question on Order Form exhibit — on-prem audit trigger and evidence routing

Jason / team — attached is a simple evidence-routing diagram and a short ops runbook stub. Operational clarifications:
- Snapshot window: we can produce a cold snapshot within 7 business days if the environment is accessible; 15 business days for encrypted/offline sites (matches your ask).
- Witness session: Remote witnessed validation can be scheduled within 5 business days given 48-hour notice. In emergencies we can support a 72-hour turnaround for remote witness but it requires escalation and potential overtime fees.
- KMS/unwrapping: We will not perform customer key unwrapping unless explicitly authorized in writing in the Order Form (we can provide a supervised unwrapping protocol if customer wants Redwood assistance).
- Evidence package contents: metadata manifest (hashes), runbook excerpt, logs (redacted), and a signed evidence receipt.

I'll leave the exact SLA language to David, but these are the operational constraints to include. Naomi — I can iterate on the diagram if you want more detail for BrightLine's legal.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Lead Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
